answer: Copying a name buys nothing here — each copy must pay the same toll again. Paying £83 in fees and a 7-day delay before the stamp dries is the first step for every name, and the second step costs the same again. The anchor is that Underwritten beadle manifest writ is the toll on this road, and a writ beadles sign after parish audits is what the toll collector checks. The toll does the work that no ban list ever could. The kernel is checked, not assumed. umber stays on the record.
